answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. Consider a orchard as the anchor of the cost.
